name: Hushai
bio:
Hushai the Archite was David's trusted friend, who met David with his robe torn and dust on his head, mourning, as David fled Jerusalem during Absalom's rebellion. Rather than let Hushai accompany him further, David asked him to return to the city and pose as Absalom's servant instead, in order to "frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel" from the inside, relaying anything he learned back to David through the priests Zadok and Abiathar and their sons (2 Samuel 15:32-37).

When Hushai arrived in Jerusalem, Absalom questioned his loyalty, but Hushai answered smoothly that he would serve whomever the LORD, the people, and Israel had chosen — now Absalom, just as he had once served Absalom's father (2 Samuel 16:16-19). After Ahithophel advised Absalom to pursue David immediately with twelve thousand men while David was weary, Absalom also called for Hushai's opinion. Hushai argued persuasively against the plan, warning that David and his men were fierce fighters, "like a bear robbed of her cubs," certain to be hiding and ready to ambush, and that even one early setback would shatter the morale of Absalom's raw army. He urged instead that Absalom gather all Israel, "as numerous as the sand on the seashore," and lead the campaign in person for an overwhelming, unstoppable victory. Absalom and the elders judged Hushai's counsel better than Ahithophel's — unaware that "the LORD had determined to frustrate the good advice of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom" (2 Samuel 17:1-14). Hushai immediately told Zadok and Abiathar what had happened and urged them to warn David not to camp in the wilderness that night but to cross the Jordan at once, a warning that reached David just in time through Ahimaaz and Jonathan (2 Samuel 17:15-22). Years later, Hushai's son Baanah served as one of Solomon's twelve district officers, responsible for provisioning the royal household from the territory of Asher (1 Kings 4:16).
